uncited: Neural and Learning-based Extraction methods generate explicit triangle meshes from implicit representations (such as Signed Distance Fields or occupancy fields) by integrating the extraction process into a differentiable computational graph.
Unlike static algorithms like Marching Cubes, these methods allow the mesh geometry to be optimized via gradient descent to fit target scalar values or visual objectives [S2, unofficial].

They set themselves apart from sibling methods by treating grid deformations and topological weights as learnable parameters, enabling the resolution of topological ambiguities and the production of high-fidelity surfaces directly from neural network outputs [977-mise-meshing-isosurfaces-by-extracting.md][3669-flexicubes.md].

All methods in this family operate on a discretized domain, typically a regular grid (Cartesian, octree, or tetrahedral) where each cell contains scalar values or occupancy states at its vertices or centers.
**Surface Determination**: A criterion is applied to identify surface locations.
In isosurface methods, this involves comparing scalar values against a threshold (isovalue) to detect sign changes or equality [30-isosurface-extraction.md].
In blocky meshing, this involves checking occupancy states or material IDs to identify exposed boundaries [31-blocky-meshing.md].
**Mesh Coherence**: Adjacent primitives are merged or connected to form a coherent mesh, often requiring vertex merging to avoid duplicates and ensure watertightness [30-isosurface-extraction.md].
The family originates from the need to bridge the gap between implicit neural representations (like NeRFs and SDFs) and explicit polygonal meshes for downstream applications.
Early work focused on static extraction from NeRF density fields [4104-nerf-density-field-mesh-extraction.md].
The introduction of differentiable extraction, such as MISE [977-mise-meshing-isosurfaces-by-extracting.md], allowed for adaptive sampling.

Subsequent developments like FlexiCubes [3669-flexicubes.md] and Differentiable Marching Cubes [9774-differentiable-marching-cubes.md] enabled end-to-end training of geometry by making the extraction process differentiable with respect to grid parameters.

Ground truth generation methods [3820-ground-truth-generation-for-neural-marching-cubes.md] were developed to train CNNs for fast inference, replacing the differentiable optimization step with a learned approximation.
